title: Flow as a Process-Related Therapeutic Factor in Psychotherapy and Expressive Therapy
summary: This study investigates whether patients experience a state of deep absorption ("flow") during psychotherapy and expressive-therapy sessions (dance/movement therapy, writing therapy), and whether this is related to their well-being during treatment. Participants fill in short questionnaires as part of their regular inpatient treatment. The aim is to better understand how and why these forms of therapy work.
conditions: Psychosomatic and psychological disorders in adult inpatients or day-clinic patients (including anxiety disorders, depressive disorders, somatoform disorders; ICD-10: F40–F45, F48, F50, F52, F59)

interventions.name: Adult patients with psychosomatic and psychological disorders (incl. anxiety disorders, depressive disorders, somatoform disorders) receiving inpatient/day-clinic treatment at the Department of Psychiatry, Psychotherapy and Psychosomatic Medicine, GLG Martin Gropius Hospital Eberswalde, are surveyed

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inpatient or day-clinic treatment in the psychosomatic clinic; participation in psychotherapeutic treatment and at least one expressive-therapy session (dance/movement therapy or writing therapy); capacity to consent; sufficient German language skills to complete the questionnaires.
Exclusion criteria:
Acute suicidality or severe clinical instability; pronounced cognitive impairment; inability to complete self-report questionnaires.
